chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from al-Husayn ibn Yasar al-Mad'ini: that he heard the questioner ask al-Rida (peace be upon him)
About a man who prayed next to a man, and he stood on his left, and he did not know what to do, then he realized while he was in prayer. He said: 'Move him to his right.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida

ai.seo_question: What should an Imam do if a follower stands on his left side during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) addresses the practical jurisprudence of correcting congregational formation (*saff*) when a follower inadvertently stands on the Imam's left. The ruling to move the worshipper to the right underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining the proper hierarchical order of prayer, ensuring the Imam remains the central axis of the congregation rather than being flanked on both sides.
